rejected_rule.statement: A direct appeal in respect of a decision made by a Provincial High Court established under Article 154P of the Constitution in the exercise of appellate jurisdiction vested in it by Article 154P(3)(b) of the Constitution, will lie to the Supreme Court with leave first had and obtained.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: In view of my findings as aforesaid, I would hold that a direct appeal in respect of a decision made by a Provincial High Court established under Article 154P of the Constitution in the exercise of appellate jurisdiction vested in it by Article 154P(3)(b) of the Constitution, will lie to the Supreme Court with leave first had and obtained, and therefore, those provisions of law referred to above, clearly, oust the revisionary jurisdiction of the Court of Appeal in respect of a decision as such and therefore, a revision will not lie to the Court of Appeal from an order as such.
rejected_rule.statute_citation_verbatim: Article 154P of the Constitution, Article 154P(3)(b) of the Constitution
